doc.title: Melba Liston — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Writing since the stroke and copying her scores
summary: She has written only for Randy since; she discusses someone transcribing her pieces for Bryant and says getting music out matters more than pay.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Because so to speak it’s been at a standstill since the six or seven years you’ve been here. You’ve written some.
For Randy, but nobody else.
Didn’t you write something for Al Grey?
Things that I did for me or somebody before.
But you did five things for me that I haven’t been able to see. I’ve got to get that transcribed.
[?] is doing them.
Oh really?
She says . . .
I know she gave you a smart answer.
“How much is I getting?”
I’m going to pay her. What does she want?
I said, “You’re going to have to ask” . . .
Clora.
Because I was giving . . .
Tell her to come to me and ask – and tell me what she wants, because it’s very important that I . . .
She doesn’t know about musicians.
And friendship.
You’ve got to get your things out all over the place, and maybe one or two people will do it, but you don’t – paying is not the – that’s not it.
That’s not the issue.
It’s not the thing. It’s getting them out as fast and varied.
